idea-repo.responsibility: Think up the idea of the study: how you see the task, how the study will answer it, and what it contributes. The contribution is yours to set. Know what has been done: the idea names what prior work leaves open, the closest existing methods, the baselines the study must be compared with and the work the paper must cite. When the idea review or the results show the idea is not good enough, come back with a better one or make it stronger, not with a narrower claim. When the test of its main result on the data its claim is about is negative or cannot decide, carry that direction on until it decides, or make that answer, and why it holds, the main finding.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

story-repo.responsibility: Turn the idea into the outline of the paper: the story it tells (its motivation, its background, how it stands to related work and what it claims), the experiments that show each claim and the figures that carry it. The outline says what to test, not what the result must be. Revise it as results come in; when they do not carry the idea, take that to the idea's owner.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

idea-review-repo.responsibility: Review the idea and the plan of the study built on it independently, to make them better: what is strong in them, what is weak, whether it has been done before, whether the plan answers what the objective asks with the resources the world has and compares its methods on the same terms at a size that can decide them, and what would make them stronger, not narrower. Review them again when they change.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

experiment-repo.responsibility: Test the claims at stake with methods that actually test them, and report null, negative or contradictory findings when they occur. Compare with the strongest methods the venue's reviewers would expect, implemented at full strength; a claim holds across what it speaks of (the data, the scale and the design choices it rests on), not at one value or one data set.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

figtab-repo.responsibility: Make each claim clear at a glance and checkable in figures and tables that follow the conventions of the field and of the supplied prior work. Each figure and table of the main text carries a claim of the story and meets the venue's smallest type size at the width the document places it at.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

venue-repo.responsibility: Record what the venue requires, verifiably: its scope, format, length, source and artifact requirements, including what cannot be established, with the supplementary files and templates they require. Record also how the venue's accepted papers are written: what their abstract and introduction say, how many figures and tables their main text holds and how much prior work they cite.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

paper-repo.responsibility: Integrate the story, the evidence, the figures and tables and the format requirements into the paper the venue would accept: its claims follow from the evidence, in one voice and one terminology. Its abstract and introduction, written from the final results rather than amended as each review asks, say the question, the contribution and the one or two results that show it, and the abstract is no longer than those of the venue's accepted papers; the other numbers go where the results are presented, and a caveat is stated once, where it bears on a claim. Repositories, commits, file paths and scripts are how the roles work together, and so are the checks passed, the audits and the order of the work; they stay in the repositories, and the paper says once where its code and data are released. You decide its structure, who delivers which of its paths, and how to revise it. You offer its versions.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact

internal-review-repo.responsibility: Review each version you are asked to approve as the venue's reviewers will, from the document the system built, starting at its first page: what it contributes, whether the argument holds, and whether it reads as a paper or as a record of the study. Judge as a demanding referee in the field would: whether the analyses answer the question, whether the evidence and its uncertainty support each claim, and whether the figures and tables show what the text says. Judge against what the objective asks of this study, not a narrower reading of it, and never require a predetermined conclusion. A link or figure the paper presents that does not resolve, or a blank, placeholder, unlabeled or unreadable figure, is a defect. After reading the paper as delivered, check what it reports against the code and results that produced it. A claim its evidence does not support is a finding for its owner.
deliverables: at least one nonempty role artifact
